text: Now the main point of what we are saying is this: we have such a high priest, one who has taken his seat at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens,
a minister in the sanctuary and in the true tent, which the Lord set up, not any human being.
Every high priest is appointed to offer gifts and sacrifices; therefore it was necessary for this one also to have something to offer.
Now if he were on earth, he would not be a priest at all, since there are already those who offer the gifts prescribed by the law.

versions.text: If he were on earth, he would not be a priest at all, since there are already those who offer the gifts prescribed by the law.
versions.explanation: The connective μὲν οὖν is dropped. Restoring a light "Now" preserves the argument's flow from verse 3 and helps the sentence begin more smoothly when read aloud.

text: They serve a copy and shadow of the heavenly things, just as Moses was instructed when he was about to erect the tent: "See that you make everything according to the pattern shown you on the mountain."

versions.text: They serve at a sanctuary that is a copy and shadow of the heavenly one, just as Moses was instructed when he was about to erect the tent: "See that you make everything according to the pattern shown you on the mountain."
versions.explanation: The Greek says they serve "a copy and shadow of the heavenly things" (τῶν ἐπουρανίων, plural). The current rendering inserts "at a sanctuary" (not in the text) and narrows the plural to "the heavenly one."

text: But as it is, Christ has obtained a ministry as far superior as the covenant he mediates is better, since it is established on better promises.
For if that first covenant had been faultless, there would have been no need to look for a second.
For God finds fault with them when he says: "Look, the days are coming, declares the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah.

versions.text: But God finds fault with them when he says: "The days are coming, declares the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah.
versions.explanation: γάρ is explanatory ("for"), giving the reason for verse 7's statement. Rendering it as "But" reverses the logical connection between the two verses.

versions.text: For God finds fault with them when he says:
versions.explanation: The entire quotation from Jeremiah has been dropped: Ἰδοὺ ἡμέραι ἔρχονται, λέγει κύριος, καὶ συντελέσω ἐπὶ τὸν οἶκον Ἰσραὴλ καὶ ἐπὶ τὸν οἶκον Ἰούδα διαθήκην καινήν. Without it the introductory formula "when he says" dangles and verse 9 has no antecedent covenant to contrast with. The interjection Ἰδοὺ ("Look") is also restored, and the opening quotation mark is left unclosed since the quotation continues into verse 9.

text: It will not be like the covenant I made with their fathers on the day I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt, for they did not remain faithful to my covenant, and so I turned away from them, declares the Lord.

This is the covenant I will make with the house of Israel after those days, declares the Lord: I will put my laws in their minds and write them on their hearts. I will be their God, and they will be my people.
No longer will anyone teach his neighbor or his brother, saying, 'Know the Lord,' because they will all know me, from the least of them to the greatest.
For I will be merciful toward their iniquities, and I will remember their sins no more."

versions.text: For I will be merciful toward their wrongdoing, and I will remember their sins no more."
versions.explanation: ἀδικίαις is plural and parallels the plural "sins" in the second clause; the singular "wrongdoing" flattens the pairing that gives the line its rhythm.

text: By speaking of a new covenant, he has made the first one obsolete; and what is obsolete and aging is about to disappear.
